beats.say: Grab a honey badger, and it spins around inside its own skin.
Its skin is thick, and super loose.
So it can twist right around, and bite back.
That tough skin shrugs off bee stings.
So it rips open beehives, for the baby bees.
It also eats scorpions, and even snakes.
It even has a built in resistance to snake venom.
About the size of a small dog. Afraid of nothing.
It lives in Africa, the Middle East, and India.
Those front claws dig burrows, fast.
It sleeps in a hole by day.
At night, it trots out to hunt.
It digs out mice, lizards, and roots.
And like a skunk, it can let out a stink.
One badger named Stoffel lived at a rescue center.
He kept breaking out of his pen.
He stacked logs and rocks, to climb the wall.
He even learned to open the gate.
His escapes were filmed for a TV documentary.
Would you try to keep one as a pet?
A small dog in a baggy coat, that bites back from inside it.
